findings.inputs: inventory.md folder tree; scratch model/ directory listing
findings.expected: Inputs, functions, and outputs separated with human-readable names; ideally a recognized HE-modeling or R-package layout
findings.observed: Rubric level: Adequate. A DARTH-style layout is used consistently: numbered pipeline scripts (01_data_prep.R ... 15_save_snapshot.R) in analysis/, reusable single-aim functions in functions/, diagnostic/validation scripts in tests/, deprecated code isolated in archive/ (confirmed unreferenced by any source() call), and self-contained Quarto reports/vignettes/technical_docs subfolders. File names are human-readable throughout. Does not reach Advanced because the repo is not organized as an installable R package (no DESCRIPTION/NAMESPACE/R/ package-style layout) despite CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md documenting the intended structure in detail.
findings.recommended_fix: No action required for Adequate; to reach Advanced, consider packaging functions/ as an installable R package (DESCRIPTION + NAMESPACE) if long-term maintenance value justifies the overhead.

findings.test: CHAOS consistent style / DARTH prefix coverage
findings.inputs: Manual read of model_fun.R (515 lines), calculate_outcomes.R (94 lines), model_configs.R (171 lines), 07_basecase_input_parameters.R:51-98, psa_functions.R:1-60
findings.expected: DARTH prefixes (v_, m_, a_, l_, df_, n_, p_, r_, hr_/rr_/or_, c_, u_, q_) applied consistently to objects of the corresponding type; tidyverse spacing/naming
findings.observed: Rubric level: Adequate (not Advanced). Domain parameter objects follow DARTH prefixes very consistently and correctly: l_params_base, p_os/p_pfs (survival curve lists), p_pf/p_p/p_d (state occupancy), c_drug_nivo/c_drug_FLOX/c_test_CT/c_other_visit (costs), u_np/u_p (utilities), v_dw_c/v_dw_e (discount-weight vectors), l_nivo/l_FLOX_exp/l_CT (treatment-schedule vectors). However coverage is incomplete for generic locals: plain vectors/data frames/matrices are frequently left unprefixed, e.g. `strategies`, `time_points` (07_basecase_input_parameters.R:2-3, should be v_strategies/v_time_points), `cost_matrix`/`effect_matrix` (psa_functions.R:50, should be m_cost/m_effect), `samples`/`dist_info` in generate_psa_samples (psa_functions.R:9-13), and constants ALL_STRATEGIES/ALL_BIOMARKERS (model_configs.R:28,31) use SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE rather than a v_ prefix. This is a coverage gap, not an inconsistency-within-domain-objects problem -- the prefixes that ARE used are used correctly and uniformly.
findings.recommended_fix: Extend DARTH prefixing to local vectors/matrices/data frames (v_, m_, df_) in psa_functions.R, evppi_functions.R, and the analysis scripts; this is cosmetic and safe to do incrementally without touching calculation logic.

findings.target: all 207 user-defined functions across scripts/R and scripts/QMD (per inventory.json)
findings.inputs: inventory.json functions[] roxygen field, aggregated by folder via Rscript/jsonlite
findings.expected: Inline headings, inline comments, description of model flow, and roxygen2 (or equivalent) documentation on functions
findings.observed: Rubric level: Adequate overall (inline headings + inline comments + flow description are present throughout, e.g. the header blocks in model_fun.R and model_configs.R), but roxygen2 coverage is only 30.0% (62/207) so it falls short of Advanced repo-wide. Coverage is very uneven by folder: functions/ 72.2% (39/54) -- effectively Advanced on its own; analysis/ 38.1% (8/21); QMD/report 17.5% (10/57); QMD/vignettes 9.4% (5/53); archive/ 0% (0/9); scripts/R/tests/ 0% (0/7); QMD/technical_docs 0% (0/6). The core reusable functions (functions/) are documented to a near-package standard; the pipeline scripts, tests, and report/vignette helper functions rely on plain comments only.
findings.recommended_fix: Add roxygen2 (or at minimum a structured comment block: purpose, @param-style, @return-style) to the analysis-script top-level helper functions and to scripts/R/tests/*.R; QMD report/vignette helpers are lower priority since each document is self-contained and their purpose is usually locally evident.

findings.inputs: inventory.md entry-point candidates and dependency graph; AGENTS.md File Organization Principles
findings.expected: Model coded as multiple, consecutive, numbered functions with distinct aims, ideally with prepare/run/analyze separation
findings.observed: Rubric level: Advanced. The pipeline is fully modularized and numbered (01_data_prep -> 03_biomarker_strategies = prepare; 06-09 = fit/run model; 10-14 = analyze/sensitivity; 15 = snapshot), each single-purpose function is centralized in functions/ with a clear call graph (get_current_model_config -> get_strategies/get_biomarkers -> model_fun -> calculate_outcomes, per inventory.md dependency graph), and cross-cutting concerns (PSA sampling, EVPPI, scenario analysis, snapshot comparison) are each isolated in their own function file (psa_functions.R, evppi_functions.R, scenario_analysis.R, snapshot_utils.R).

findings.inputs: environment.md package table (37 packages, all flagged 'undeclared', renv.lock present: FALSE, DESCRIPTION present: FALSE); directory listing of scratch model/ (no README.md, no LICENSE, no DESCRIPTION, no renv.lock, no .Rproj)
findings.expected: Package & dependencies rubric: at minimum packages listed with versions in README (Adequate); lockfile such as renv.lock for Advanced. Starting point/README rubric: goal, contact, install guidance present.
findings.observed: Rubric level: Absent-to-Basic. No renv.lock, no DESCRIPTION, and no README.md are present anywhere in the reviewed model/ copy, so package versions are entirely unpinned -- all 37 detected packages (flexsurv, survival, dampack, darthtools, mvtnorm, etc.) are loaded via pacman::p_load() inline in each script/report with no version constraints. AGENTS.md (the repo's instruction file, not shipped as README) does document required packages and run order in detail, which substitutes for some of the 'Run guidance' rubric content, but the CHAOS rubric specifically expects this in a README and expects a restorable lockfile for the top rubric level, neither of which is present. NOTE: `git log` on the parent repository shows README.md exists in the last commit (4e55627) but is deleted in the current working tree (git status shows 'D README.md'); this looks like an uncommitted local deletion in the source workspace rather than a genuine repository decision, so the Absent verdict may be a snapshot artifact -- recommend the scorer re-check against a clean checkout before weighting this heavily.
findings.recommended_fix: Add an renv.lock (or equivalent) pinning exact versions of all 37 packages so PSA/EVPPI/CEA numeric results can be exactly regenerated on a new machine; restore/keep README.md (present in git history) with package + version list and install guidance; add a minimal DESCRIPTION even without turning the repo into an installable package, purely to declare dependencies machine-readably.

findings.target: data/tidy/ caches vs UTILITY_SOURCE default; data/sensitive/ and data/tidy/METIMMOX.rds availability
findings.inputs: 02_setup_and_global_variables.R:59-60 (UTILITY_SOURCE <- 1, utility_source_label <- 'correct'); data/tidy/ listing (sampling_models_n5000_full.rds, psa_obj_correct.rds, psa_params_correct.rds, evppi_results_correct.RData, scenario_evppi_results_correct.rds); data/sensitive/ and data/tidy/METIMMOX.rds present in scratch copy
findings.expected: Base case (and ideally full) results replicate from the documented run order without hidden manual steps
findings.observed: Rubric level (static, not executed here): consistent with 'Base case / Full' reproducibility WITHIN this scratch environment -- the cached sampling/PSA/EVPPI/scenario objects are all suffixed '_correct', which matches the repo's default UTILITY_SOURCE = 1 ('correct') in 02_setup_and_global_variables.R, so a render using documented defaults should load caches successfully rather than silently regenerating with mismatched settings. HOWEVER this reproducibility is NOT available to a fresh public git clone: the confidential METIMMOX.rds and data/sensitive/*.xlsx trial files are present in this scratch copy (needed to run the model) but AGENTS.md states they are intentionally excluded from the repository proper (git-ignored, per the real repo's .gitignore), and CS-005 already notes packages are unpinned. This is a data-governance decision, clearly documented in AGENTS.md, not a hidden defect -- flagged here only so the reproducibility rubric level is scored with the caveat attached, since 'Full' reproducibility requires both code AND data AND pinned packages, and only the first is guaranteed to ship with the repository.
findings.recommended_fix: No fix needed for the data-confidentiality design (appropriate for clinical trial data); actual base-case execution and numeric replication should be confirmed by the black-box subagent's run, which this static review defers to. Document in the README (once restored, see CS-005) that a data use agreement / synthetic data are required for outsiders to reproduce results end-to-end.

findings.test: TECH-VER Stage 5 -- duplicate code / DRY violation
findings.inputs: inventory.md duplicate_definitions list (29 names incl. fit_firth_cox, extract_coxphf_results, run_wilcox_test, run_fisher_test, run_mh_test, run_firth_cox_test, run_firth_logistic_test, run_permutation_test, complete_data, fmt_hr, fmt_or, fmt_num); byte-level diff of fit_firth_cox()/extract_coxphf_results() bodies in clinical_effectiveness.qmd:89-134 vs forrest-plot.qmd:60-85 (confirmed identical)
findings.expected: Shared logic centralized in functions/ and sourced, not copy-pasted across independent documents (or, if intentionally duplicated for self-containment, kept in verified sync)
findings.observed: 29 function names are defined more than once across the codebase. Spot-checked fit_firth_cox and extract_coxphf_results: currently byte-identical between clinical_effectiveness.qmd and forrest-plot.qmd, so no drift exists today. But per inventory.md's own caveat ('last source() wins silently'), and because these are copy-pasted rather than sourced from one place, a future bug fix applied to one copy (e.g. the maxit=500 Firth-convergence fix noted in the code comment) will silently NOT propagate to the sibling copy unless the author remembers to update both. This matches AGENTS.md's documented design intent for the vignettes/reports ('self-contained', re-source dependencies independently) so it is a deliberate tradeoff, not an oversight -- scored as a latent-drift risk rather than a live defect.
findings.recommended_fix: Move the statistical-test helpers (fit_firth_cox, extract_coxphf_results, run_wilcox_test family, fmt_hr/fmt_or/fmt_num/complete_data) into a shared scripts/R/functions/*.R file sourced by both the report and its dependent vignette, or add a comment at each duplicate site cross-referencing its sibling so a future editor knows to update both.

findings.test: TECH-VER Stage 5 -- error-masking patterns (code-quality note, not correctness)
findings.inputs: grep counts: tryCatch( x43, suppressWarnings x7, try( x2, na.rm= x67, <<- x39 across scripts/R; manual read of model_fun.R:170-259 and 08_sampling.R:74-160
findings.expected: Error handling is transparent to callers, not silently substituting different data with only a warning()
findings.observed: model_fun.R wraps PSA curve generation in tryCatch(...) and, on failure, falls back to base-case survival curves while emitting only a warning() (not stop()); the fallback is tracked via an attr(result, 'fallback_used') attribute per Issue #79, and 08_sampling.R similarly falls back to the original (non-resampled) model on a per-resample basis, tracked via n_failed/failed. This is a deliberately engineered and well-commented pattern (not silent masking in the pejorative sense -- callers CAN detect it), which is better practice than typical error-masking, but it still means a PSA iteration that failed model-fitting silently contributes base-case-derived numbers to the uncertainty distribution unless the calling PSA loop actually checks the fallback attribute/failed flag on every iteration. The <<- usages (39 total) are consistently used only to escape tryCatch()/for-loop closures back to an enclosing counter or flag (e.g. fallback_used <<- TRUE, n_failed <<- n_failed + 1), not to mutate arbitrary global state -- a legitimate, narrow use of <<-.
findings.recommended_fix: Confirm (cross-reference with the black-box/white-box findings) that every caller of model_fun() in PSA mode and every consumer of sampling_models actually inspects fallback_used / n_failed / the per-sample failed flag and excludes or reports affected iterations; if any caller (e.g. 12_PSA.R, 14_scenario_EVPPIs.R) does not check it, surface that as a white-box finding rather than here.

findings.test: TECH-VER Stage 5 -- for (i in 1:n) robustness idiom
findings.inputs: grep 'for (i in 1:n' / 'for (i in 1:nrow(' across scripts/R/functions and scripts/R/analysis (10 occurrences)
findings.expected: Loop bounds constructed with seq_len()/seq_along() so a zero-length input produces zero iterations rather than the classic 1:0 -> c(1,0) R pitfall
findings.observed: Ten loops use the `for (i in 1:nrow(x))` / `for (i in 1:n_sim)` idiom instead of seq_len(nrow(x)) / seq_len(n_sim). In all inspected cases the driving quantity (n_samples, n_sim, nrow(param_combinations), nrow(dsa_ranges), nrow(scenarios_preview)) is a fixed, non-zero configuration value in the current pipeline, so this is not observed to trigger in practice, but it is a latent robustness gap if any of these tables/config vectors is ever empty (e.g. an EVPPI parameter-group filter that returns zero rows) -- the loop would then run for i in c(1, 0) or similar reversed/garbage indices instead of being skipped.
findings.recommended_fix: Replace `for (i in 1:n)` / `for (i in 1:nrow(x))` with `for (i in seq_len(n))` / `for (i in seq_len(nrow(x)))` throughout; mechanical, low-risk change.

findings.inputs: grep for 'rbind(<var>, data.frame(' inside for-loops in 11_DSA.R and create_tornado_plot.R
findings.expected: Accumulate results into a pre-sized list and combine once (do.call(rbind, list)) rather than repeatedly rbind()-ing onto a growing data frame inside a loop
findings.observed: 11_DSA.R uses the classic `df <- rbind(df, data.frame(...))` pattern inside for-loops at 5 locations (and create_tornado_plot.R at 1 location), which is O(n^2) in the number of loop iterations because each rbind copies the whole accumulated frame. Note the same file (11_DSA.R:136,239) elsewhere correctly uses the pre-allocated-list + do.call(rbind, list) pattern, so the codebase clearly knows the efficient idiom -- this is inconsistency rather than a systemic gap. Given DSA parameter counts are small (tens, not thousands, of rows), real runtime impact is negligible; flagged as a style/efficiency inconsistency rather than a performance problem.
findings.recommended_fix: For consistency with the pre-allocated-list pattern already used at 11_DSA.R:136 and 11_DSA.R:239, replace the growing-rbind loops with append-to-list + a single do.call(rbind, ...) at the end. Purely cosmetic/performance; no behavior change expected.

findings.test: TECH-VER Stage 5 -- naming drift / dead-code hygiene
findings.inputs: File header ('SINGLE-MODEL CEA HELPER FUNCTIONS...Functions for running and summarizing the single joint economic model') vs filename multi_model_cea.R; AGENTS.md ('There is no model-structure switch or multi-structure comparison layer')
findings.expected: Filenames match current content/purpose after refactors
findings.observed: multi_model_cea.R is now, by its own header comment and by AGENTS.md's description of the current single-model architecture, single-model tooling (run_basecase, load_psa_cache, create_ceac_plot for the one joint economic model). The filename is a leftover from a prior multi-model-comparison architecture that was refactored away (per git log context: 'refactor stage 6/7' commits visible in the parent repo). Purely a naming-hygiene issue; does not affect correctness.
findings.recommended_fix: Rename to e.g. cea_helpers.R or single_model_cea.R to match its documented single-model scope, updating the handful of source() call sites.

findings.inputs: resolve_best_distributions() body: exists('models', envir = .GlobalEnv); get('models', envir = .GlobalEnv)
findings.expected: Functions declare their data dependencies as parameters where practical, rather than reaching into .GlobalEnv, to keep them independently testable
findings.observed: resolve_best_distributions() takes only a `biomarker` argument but reads the fitted-model comparison object `models` directly out of .GlobalEnv via exists()/get() rather than accepting it as a parameter. This mirrors a documented, intentional pattern used throughout the script-based (non-package) pipeline (AGENTS.md explicitly describes sourcing scripts into a shared global environment), so it is consistent with the codebase's overall design rather than an isolated slip -- but it does mean the function cannot be unit-tested in isolation without first populating .GlobalEnv$models, and silently falls back to a hardcoded 'weibull' default (with only a cat() warning, not a stop()) if `models` is missing or malformed.
findings.recommended_fix: Pass `models` as an explicit parameter to resolve_best_distributions() (with a default that reads from .GlobalEnv for backward compatibility, e.g. `models = get0('models', envir = .GlobalEnv)`), so the function can be called and tested with an arbitrary models object.

findings.inputs: Read file headers of compare_snapshots.R, diagnose_prediction_failures.R, test_psa_error_rate.R, test_sampling_convergence_rate.R, test_sex_variable_fix.R, test_sim_idx_validation.R, tlr.R, fit_independent_biomarker_models.R; grep for 'testthat' across scripts/ (0 hits)
findings.expected: N/A rubric item directly, but relevant to reproducibility/verification maturity -- automated assertions vs manual inspection
findings.observed: No testthat (or other formal test-runner) usage anywhere in the repo. scripts/R/tests/ contains ad-hoc diagnostic/verification scripts that print cat() output for manual inspection (e.g. test_sex_variable_fix.R, test_sim_idx_validation.R) rather than asserting with stopifnot()/testthat expectations or integrating with CI. tests/tlr.R additionally duplicates data-loading logic from 01_data_prep.R (reads the raw METIMMOX Excel file directly and calls rm(list=ls())), rather than reusing 01_data_prep.R -- a second, smaller instance of the DRY concern in CS-007.
findings.recommended_fix: Not required by CHAOS/TECH-VER directly, but consider migrating the highest-value scripts (test_sim_idx_validation.R, test_sex_variable_fix.R) to testthat::test_that() with explicit expect_error()/expect_equal() assertions so they can run unattended in CI and fail loudly rather than requiring a human to read cat() output.

findings.test: Inventory false-positive check -- environment.md package table
findings.target: environment.md package table row 'pkg ... not installed ... MISSING'
findings.inputs: grep '\bpkg\b' across scripts/ excluding p_load/package matches -> single hit at scripts/R/functions/snapshot_utils.R:31
findings.expected: Package inventory should not list loop variables as dependencies
findings.observed: The environment.md package table flags a package literally named 'pkg' as MISSING/not-installed. This is a false positive from the inventory tool's static parser: `pkg` is a for-loop variable name inside get_package_versions() (snapshot_utils.R:29-33: `for (pkg in ...) { versions[[pkg]] <- if (requireNamespace(pkg, quietly = TRUE)) ... }`), not an actual required package. No real missing dependency exists here.
findings.recommended_fix: No code fix needed. Informational note for the scorer/aggregator so the environment.md 'pkg MISSING' row is not double-counted as a real dependency gap alongside CS-005.
